facts.fact: Thankam is the queen's surgeon: a broad woman past fifty with grey hair tied in a green strip, who closes Devan's wound with clamp, needle and waxed silk.
facts.why: needed because the beat names Thankam as palace surgeon working by lamp.

facts.fact: Thankam says the spear cut the nerve behind the collarbone; the shoulder and lung will mend, but the nerve to the right hand is cut and may take a year to regrow, if the hand ever closes hard again.
facts.why: needed because the beat has the surgeon say the nerve to the hand is cut.

facts.fact: Queen Nirmala has a hand-long red welt on her left forearm from Usha's wound; she holds the lantern for Thankam, kneeling in blood.
facts.why: needed because the beat gives the queen a fresh welt and has her hold the lamp.

facts.fact: The wounded are tended in a pocket against the rock at the rear of the shelf, on a cart tarpaulin under a hooded lantern hung from a stake.
facts.why: needed to place the surgery behind the cut.

facts.fact: At dawn Kandan and Muthu turn their backs as Neela turns back, and Muthu passes her a blanket; she rests two fingers on the healing point a hand's breadth under Devan's jaw at the hollow of the throat.
facts.why: needed to stage the turning back and the marma point without new rules.
